applies_why: The judge text evaluates a collision at Matthew 1:20 by setting the challenger's chain answer from [DR3] against the defender's chain answers from [CR2] and [CR3], rather than deciding by the verse's wording alone.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: weighs chain against chain by footing — I weighed whether this requires resolving which chain is stronger, or permits underdetermined when both chains supply opposing footings; I used the latter because the text names both chains' answers.
why: The judge did not require Matthew 1:20 to state the contrary in its own words, but instead treated the challenger's and defender's competing chain readings as leaving the point underdetermined.
